Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: High latency and errors from Redwood inference since 07:30 PT

David —

We started seeing a sharp uptick in generator latency across our transaction stream around 07:30 PT. Median p95 jumped from ~250ms to ~1.8s and error rates climbed to ~3.2% on /v1/generate. This is hitting our checkout flow and causing timeouts at the client.

We reported through the support channel but want an executive touch — OrbitAI is in a weekly feature launch window and this is customer visible. Can you confirm receipt and share an ETA for mitigation?

Attaching a short telemetry export.

Thanks,
Laura
VP Product, OrbitAI

Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 08:27:05 -0800
Subject: Re: High latency and errors from Redwood inference since 07:30 PT

David / team —

Quick findings from initial triage:
- Symptom: rising tail latency and a correlated spike in 5xx errors on the v1/generate route. p50 unchanged.
- Affected region: us-west-2 host pool serving OrbitAI (dedicated pool).
- Likely cause: excessive KV cache churn when a new batch of long-context prompts hit simultaneously; we've seen similar contention when sequence lengths spike during checkout.
- Current mitigation in progress: we pushed a temporary routing policy to divert smaller token-count traffic to a sibling variant and slowed background prefetch.

Marissa — the pool shows one node with elevated NVLink errors and transient CUDA kernel restarts; I'm preparing a fallback plan to drain that node and scale up a healthy reserve. If the node fails further, we should auto-failover to the secondary pool.

I'll join the 09:00 PT bridge with telemetry.

—Karthik
Sr. Director, Serving Engineering

Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 08:58:40 -0800
Subject: Re: High latency and errors from Redwood inference since 07:30 PT

Status update ahead of exec bridge:
- Timeline: root pool pressure started at ~07:28 PT; NVLink error counts increased at 07:34 PT on node id rwd-usw2-gpu-19.
- Action taken: drained rwd-usw2-gpu-19, rotated traffic; we provisioned two standby nodes and applied an emergency configuration to tighten batching (= smaller max batch) for Orbit routes.
- Observed effect: p95 decreased from 1.8s to ~650ms for routed traffic; global error rate reduced from 3.2% to 0.8% but some checkout flows still time out due to in-flight requests on affected node.
- Next steps in the bridge: execute controlled node replacement and a short rolling restart of the variant with the new kernel patch.

I'll present the above on the 09:00 PT bridge and propose a customer-facing ETA of 90 minutes for full restoration (contingent on successful node replacement).

Marissa
Head of Production Reliability

Thank you for flagging this so quickly and sharing the telemetry. We briefed our operations and engineering leaders and have an active remediation in progress. Short summary:
- Initial mitigation applied (traffic diversion and node drain) — partial improvement seen.
- Root cause (under investigation): GPU interconnect errors exacerbated by a burst of long-context requests causing KV cache churn and batch contention.
- Customer ETA: our current plan is to complete a node replacement and rolling variant restart within ~90 minutes; we'll confirm earlier if we observe full recovery sooner.

Action items for OrbitAI: please share any changes to prompt patterns or big job runs in the last hour, and confirm whether you can toggle a short client-side retry/backoff for checkout requests until we clear the queue.

We'll update you at +30 minutes or sooner if anything changes.

-David

Subject: Post-mortem snapshot: OrbitAI Shoreline event — customer update ready

Orbit leadership —

Final note from the bridge: full traffic normalization observed at ~16:10 PT after node replacement and rolling restart + kernel patch; p95 returned to baseline (~240ms) and error rate fell to <0.1%.

Customer-facing summary (ready to send):
- What happened: between 07:28–08:40 PT an NVLink-related hardware fault on a single dedicated node coupled with an unusual burst of long-context requests caused KV cache churn and elevated tail latency and 5xx errors for OrbitAI.
- What we did: isolated and drained the failing node, scaled healthy standby capacity, applied a temporary routing policy to reduce batch sizes, and deployed a targeted kernel patch to improve NVLink resilience; completed a rolling restart of the variant.
- Impact: partial mitigation at ~08:58 PT; full restoration and validation completed at ~16:10 PT. We confirmed end-to-end checkout flows and telemetry.
- Next steps: 1) Post-incident engineering ticket to harden cache eviction heuristics (owner: Karthik), 2) hardware telemetry ingest improvements (owner: Marissa), 3) joint review with OrbitAI scheduled for Mon 16 Nov 10:00 PT.

Suggested customer note (two lines):
"We identified and fixed a hardware-related failure in a dedicated node that, together with a transient traffic pattern, increased latency and error rates this morning. We have replaced the node and deployed a fix; normal service has been restored and we have scheduled a technical follow-up with your team."

If there are no edits, I'll send this to Laura + TJ and copy Legal/Finance.

Hannah
Director, Customer Success
OrbitAI customer lead — Redwood Inference
